answer: Resist sybils with copper-bound hardware identity: one agent, one physical chip. First, each identity registers a TPM attestation proving a unique device whose copper-etched serial is signed by the manufacturer. Second, the registry rejects any serial seen before and holds the identity on a 14-day probation ridge limited to microtasks. Third, proven fraud bricks the serial for a year and slashes the $40 device bond. Forging 10,000 identities needs 10,000 chips, $400,000 in bonds, and 60 days of staged purchases. Like a canyon that admits only one river, one chip carries only one voice.
